title_prefix: The version record is written once at cr
mechanism: The VERSION half is confirmed. create-wallet writes one "version" record holding +wallet-client-version+ (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1004-1005) and that is the only reference to +wdb-key-version+ in the tree outside its own defconstant (src/wallet/wallet-store.lisp:40) and a byte-round-trip test (tests/wallet/wallet-tests.lisp:192): %load-wallet-records has no branch for it in either pass, so an unmatched record simply falls through the cond, and nothing ever refreshes it. Core reads it first thing in WalletBatch::LoadWallet -- last_client starts at CLIENT_VERSION, is overwritten from DBKeys::VERSION, and is logged as "Last client version = %d" (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1122-1125 (LoadWallet begins at :1115)); it is then threaded into LoadLegacyWalletRecords and LoadDescriptorWalletRecords, where last_client > CLIENT_VERSION is what picks "The wallet might have been created on a newer version. " over "The database might be corrupted..." (walletdb.cpp:782-783); and on a clean load Core rewrites it whenever it was absent or stale: if (!has_last_client || last_client != CLIENT_VERSION) WriteVersion(CLIENT_VERSION) (walletdb.cpp:1177-1178). We have no equivalent of any of the three -- there is no "Last client version" log line anywhere in src/. The MINVERSION half is REFUTED: at d3056bc DBKeys::MINVERSION is declared in walletdb.h:74 and defined in walletdb.cpp:47 and read or written NOWHERE in Core's source or tests (grep over refs/bitcoin/src and refs/bitcoin/test returns exactly those two lines), so our dead +wdb-key-minversion+ constant mirrors Core's dead constant rather than diverging from it. Core's TOO_NEW class at d3056bc comes from unknown non-tolerable wallet FLAGS (walletdb.cpp:449-453), not from a version record, and we do have that branch (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1056-1064, "Unknown wallet flags" at :1063).
consequence: The wallet cannot tell a too-new file from a corrupt one, so the load-time diagnostic Core words differently for the two cases does not exist here, and the on-disk stamp is wrong forever once anything changes it or fails to write it: a wallet loaded with 999999 on disk is still 999999 after unload, and a wallet whose version record is missing never gets one. Purely diagnostic -- nothing is mis-loaded, the wallet loads identically in every case -- so S3. No Core functional test asserts on the version record; the wording it selects appears in wallet_*.py nowhere.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-wallet-s3, warm container; probe build/ga11probe/p4.lisp (bitcoin-lisp.tests::ga11-p5), regtest wallet "wv", records read and written directly against the wallet's LevelDB between unloadwallet and loadwallet. Results: +wallet-client-version+ = 100 (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:58, = bl.ser:+client-version+ 0.1.0 under Core's own 10000*major + 100*minor + build formula, clientversion.h:26-29); version record after create = 100; minversion record after create = NIL (never written); the created wallet's record types are exactly (activeexternalspk activeinternalspk bestblock bestblock_nomerkle flags version walletdescriptor walletdescriptorcache walletdescriptorkey walletdescriptorlhcache). (1) version set to 999999 -> loadwallet succeeds with no warning, and after unload the record still reads 999999 (Core would have rewritten it to CLIENT_VERSION). (2) version record deleted -> loadwallet succeeds, and after unload the record is still absent (Core writes CLIENT_VERSION when !has_last_client). (3) a minversion record of 999999 added -> loadwallet succeeds and the record is untouched, which is also what Core does. (4) Positive control that the diagnostic is unreachable, not merely differently worded: with version 999999 on disk AND a truncated walletdescriptor record -- the exact combination whose message Core words "The wallet might have been created on a newer version" -- the reply is (-32603 "Internal error: Invalid index 159 for (SIMPLE-ARRAY (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8) (159))..."). Core at d3056bc: walletdb.cpp:47, :1115-1125, :782-783, :1176-1178; walletdb.h:74; wallet.cpp:2391 (TOO_NEW's message) and walletdb.cpp:449-453 (its only producer); clientversion.h:26-29.
fix_shape: Port the three uses of DBKeys::VERSION and leave MINVERSION alone, since Core does. In %load-wallet-records, read the version record before the record loop into a last-client value defaulting to +wallet-client-version+, log it once at the wallet log level the way Core's "Last client version = %d" does, and thread it to the walletdescriptor branch so the failure text 69862ba9 asks for can choose between Core's "The wallet might have been created on a newer version. " and "The database might be corrupted or the software version is not compatible with one of your wallet descriptors. " on last-client > +wallet-client-version+. Then, at the end of a load that produced no error -- Core is explicit that any corruption skips the rewrite so as not to make it worse (walletdb.cpp:1174-1178) -- write the record back when it was absent or differs from +wallet-client-version+. A regression test must cover the absent case as well as the stale one, since they are separate branches of Core's condition and the current code fails both identically.
